claims.hypothesis: Does the dependence of jet mass-loss rate on accretion rate differ between young molecular-jet sources and T Tauri stars?
claims.experiment: Separate logarithmic fits of jet mass-loss rate versus accretion rate for the two groups
claims.result: Slope ~0.40 for molecular jets versus ~0.57 for T Tauri stars
claims.finding: Younger objects accrete at higher rates but eject a smaller fraction of that mass; relative mass-loss efficiency increases toward the T Tauri stage

evidence.quote: The molecular jets show relatively shallow slopes ($\alpha$$\sim$0.40) compared to T Tauri stars ($\alpha$$\sim$0.57).
This implies that younger objects tend to accrete at higher rates but eject smaller fraction of that mass.

claims.hypothesis: Can extinction explain the high incidence of monopolar protostellar jets?
claims.experiment: Compare SiO jet monopolarity at millimeter wavelengths with expected extinction effects
claims.result: Nearly half of protostars with SiO jets appear monopolar at millimeter wavelengths
claims.finding: Extinction alone cannot explain it, suggesting intrinsic launching asymmetries

evidence.quote: Yet nearly half of protostars with SiO jets appear monopolar at millimeter wavelengths (cite: 2024AJ....167...72D).
suggesting intrinsic launching asymmetries, possibly linked to magnetic field geometry or star–disk interactions.

claims.hypothesis: Does jet episodicity depend on protostellar luminosity?
claims.experiment: Compare episodicity timescales with bolometric luminosity and envelope mass (Figure 6)
claims.result: No clear dependence on luminosity; relation to envelope mass is not straightforward
claims.finding: Luminosity alone does not reliably trace evolutionary status; correlations remain weak or statistically inconclusive

evidence.quote: the episodicities do not show any clear dependence on luminosity, most likely because luminosity alone does not reliably trace evolutionary status.
Although correlations with luminosity and envelope mass remain weak or statistically inconclusive

claims.hypothesis: Can observations discriminate between X-wind, disk-wind and stellar-wind launching models?
claims.experiment: Review of recent ALMA and JWST observations of jets and outflows
claims.result: Signatures of the models often overlap and no single model explains the diversity of observations
claims.finding: The launching mechanism is not yet disentangled

evidence.quote: However, distinguishing between these models observationally remains challenging, as signatures often overlap.
